turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, in you come. What's the problem today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hi, sorry, the car park was mad. It's Leo, he's just turned three. He's been crying half the night and yanking on his ear, and he only just had a cold.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Mummy, why we here?
[SEG0004] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sit down, love. Let your mum talk.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which ear?
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right. Well, actually, he grabs the right one. I thought left for a second this morning but no, it's the right.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many days?
[SEG0008] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um. I can't date it. Since the cold eased, maybe Sunday, or the weekend before that, around the show, or after. I keep mixing it up.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0010] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No fever at all.
[SEG0011] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, that's not true. I had him yesterday arvo and he was hot. Hot on the forehead, I'm not imagining it.
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Mum. He was warm from the crying. I checked him later and he was fine. So, no fever.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thermometer?
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Couldn't find it. I'd still put it at thirty eight point five, easy.
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You can't invent thirty eight point five, Mum. Nobody actually measured it.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Nose? Cough?
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Snotty, yeah, for a few days before the ear. Cough at night, wet sounding. Cold's on the way out, I think.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Diarrhoea?
[SEG0021] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nappies, I mean, he's in undies now, poos are normal. Sorry.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Eating and drinking?
[SEG0023] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Off his food. He'll drink milk and water. Not heaps, but he's drinking.
[SEG0024] person_3 (PATIENT): No!
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Leo. Ear sore?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0027] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He'll say no to you. He's anxious. He was beside himself at two in the morning.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Rash today?
[SEG0029] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Nothing on the skin now.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicine allergies?
[SEG0031] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm not sure. Long ago, don't ask me the date, he had amoxicillin and he got a rash, maybe. Might've been the virus. I really can't say.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): And you stopped it?
[SEG0033] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We stopped it, yeah, and I never gave it again. Blotchy, I think. He might've been one, or younger. It's a blur.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Food allergies?
[SEG0035] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No food ones. Not that I know of.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): What's that? Hurt?
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Light for your ear. On Mum's lap. Hold his head still.
[SEG0038] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Will it hurt him? He hates this bit. Do I need to pin his arms?
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Just the head. Right drum is red and bulging. Left drum looks clear. Throat's a bit red and the chest is clear.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Ow! No no.
[SEG0041] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I knew that ear was bad.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Temp thirty seven point two. Pulse one hundred and twenty four. Respiratory rate twenty six. Sats ninety eight percent.
[SEG0043] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is thirty seven point two okay? Is one hundred and twenty four too quick? Are we going to hospital? I need to know.
[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): Normal temp. Pulse is fine for a distressed toddler. No hospital.
[SEG0045] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So what is it? Antibiotics or not? I don't want to muck this up.
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Early middle ear infection, right side. Watch and wait. No antibiotics today.
[SEG0047] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Watch and wait, really? What if tonight's worse? What do I give him?
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): What have you used?

[SEG0049] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Children's Panadol. I think five mils, maybe, I'm not a hundred percent, it was dark. Every six hours-ish. And nurofen once last night, a hundred milligrams, I think the syringe said that.

[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Continue paracetamol, five mils, that's one hundred and twenty milligrams, every six hours. Ibuprofen one hundred milligrams with food if pain breaks through, up to three times a day.
[SEG0051] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Both together is safe? He won't get a sore tummy? What if I double up by mistake?
[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Safe at those doses. Don't double up. Food with the ibuprofen.
[SEG0053] person_3 (PATIENT): Ear. Ow. Hurts.
[SEG0054] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There you go. He says it once he forgets to be brave.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): No amoxicillin, because of that possible rash. Backup is cefalexin.
[SEG0056] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is cefalexin okay if the amoxicillin rash was real? Do we start it today or what? I'm lost.

[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not today. I'll write cefalexin, two hundred and fifty milligrams, three times a day, for five days. Only start it if he's still miserable after forty eight hours, or a proper fever shows up.
[SEG0058] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'd start it now. He was hot, I keep telling you.
[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not now. A lot of these settle on their own.
[SEG0060] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he won't swallow it? And do we come back, or ring, or what? Sorry, too many questions.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he's not better in two days, come back and see me. Sooner if he's drowsy, swelling behind the ear, or he stops drinking.
[SEG0062] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is that two days or forty eight hours? And my brother had glue ear, does Leo need a hearing test?
[SEG0063] person_1 (DOCTOR): Forty eight hours from now. We might do a hearing test if it does not settle. Not today.
[SEG0064] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That cold's been a good week and a bit, not a few days.
[SEG0065] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, the snotty nose was about four days. You're stretching it, Mum.
[SEG0066] person_1 (DOCTOR): Doesn't change today's plan. Keep him off kinder tomorrow.
[SEG0067] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He only does Tuesdays and Thursdays anyway. We're living with Mum for now, that's why she's piled in. Does the sharing germs thing matter?
[SEG0068] person_1 (DOCTOR): No. Fluids, rest, pain relief. Don't fill the cefalexin unless I said.
[SEG0069] person_3 (PATIENT): Go home? Why not?
[SEG0070] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Soon, bub. If he gets a rash on the cefalexin, what then? And can he swim Saturday? We promised the pool.
[SEG0071] person_1 (DOCTOR): Rash, stop the medicine and come in. No swimming till the ear pain's gone.
[SEG0072] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Script from the desk? I always forget where to stand.
[SEG0073] person_1 (DOCTOR): Reception. That's the lot.
[SEG0074] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oh, one more. He said his tummy was sore this morning, then he ate toast and it went. Is that connected?
[SEG0075] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it went after toast, leave it. Watch the ear.
[SEG0076] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll sit with him tonight. He'll be right.
[SEG0077] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Okay. Thanks. We'll get out of your hair.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Fever is disputed, but not present/current; later denied and temp was 37.2.
Dose and once last night supported, but status 'currently_used' is too strong from one prior dose.
bad.text: ibuprofen (dose=100 mg, frequency=once last night, indication=ear pain, status=currently_used, reported_by=family_member)

bad.reason: Conflict is between grandmother and mother, not mother denying while grandmother reports heat.
bad.text: Mother denies any fever while grandmother says the child felt hot yesterday. (type=conflicting_statement, related_entities=symptoms[5]; negative_findings[3], resolution_status=unresolved)

omissions.text: Child himself stated the ear hurts ('Ear. Ow. Hurts.').
Family member reported reduced intake details: he will drink milk and water, not heaps, but he is drinking.
Doctor explicitly advised watchful waiting/no antibiotics today for the ear infection.
Doctor clarified follow-up timing as forty-eight hours from now (not just 'two days').
Doctor advised not to fill/start the cefalexin unless instructed/only if criteria met.
There was a real disagreement about starting antibiotics now: family member wanted to start cefalexin immediately because she believed he was hot, and doctor disagreed ('Not now').
